title: Numbers, Dates & Time (数字、日期与时间)
description: Count from 0 to 100 and beyond, say your age, give dates with year-month-day order, name the days of the week, and ask and tell the time.

notes.heading: 🔢 Numbers 0–10
notes.body:
Master these eleven characters and you can build almost any number:

| Number | Character | Pinyin |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 零 | líng |
| 1 | 一 | yī |
| 2 | 二 | èr |
| 3 | 三 | sān |
| 4 | 四 | sì |
| 5 | 五 | wǔ |
| 6 | 六 | liù |
| 7 | 七 | qī |
| 8 | 八 | bā |
| 9 | 九 | jiǔ |
| 10 | 十 | shí |

💡 **Memory hooks:** 一, 二, 三 are just one, two and three horizontal lines. 八 looks like two strokes spreading apart — think 'eight legs apart'.

📎 **Key Point:** there are two words for 'two': 二 **èr** is used for counting and inside numbers (十二, 二十), while 两 **liǎng** is used before measure words: 两个人 (two people).

notes.heading: ➕ Numbers 11–99
notes.body:
Chinese numbers are completely regular — just combine the digits you know:

- **11–19**: 十 + digit → 十一 shíyī (11), 十二 shí'èr (12) … 十九 shíjiǔ (19)
- **20, 30 … 90**: digit + 十 → 二十 èrshí (20), 三十 sānshí (30) … 九十 jiǔshí (90)
- **21–99**: digit + 十 + digit → 二十一 èrshí-yī (21), 五十八 wǔshí-bā (58), 九十九 jiǔshí-jiǔ (99)

💡 **Worked Example:** 47 = 四十七 sìshí-qī — 'four ten seven'.

⚠️ **Common Mistake:** 15 is 十五 shíwǔ, never 一十五 — the 'one' before 十 is dropped for 11–19.

🔑 **How it works:** the pattern is read exactly as it is written: tens first, then units, with no exceptions.

notes.heading: 💯 Hundreds: 百 and Reading Long Numbers
notes.body:
百 **bǎi** means hundred:

- 一百 yìbǎi = 100
- 二百 èrbǎi = 200
- 三百 sānbǎi = 300
- 一百二十三 yìbǎi èrshí-sān = 123

💡 **Worked Example:** 350 = 三百五十 sānbǎi wǔshí — 'three hundred five ten'.

📎 **Key Points:**
- Phone numbers are read digit by digit: 138… = yī sān bā…
- 零 líng (0) is used inside long numbers to show a gap: 一百零五 yìbǎi líng wǔ = 105.
- Before measure words use 两 for two: 两百 liǎngbǎi (200 of something counted with a measure word), but 二百 èrbǎi when simply saying the number.

notes.heading: 🎂 Saying Your Age — 岁
notes.body:
岁 **suì** means 'years old'. The pattern is:

**我 + number + 岁。** — Wǒ shí'èr suì. (I am twelve years old.)

Add 今年 **jīnnián** (this year) to be extra clear:
我今年十二岁。Wǒ jīnnián shí'èr suì. — I am twelve this year.

Asking someone's age:

| Chinese | Pinyin | Use |
|---|---|---|
| 你几岁？ | Nǐ jǐ suì? | to children |
| 你今年几岁？ | Nǐ jīnnián jǐ suì? | to children / classmates |
| 您多大？ | Nín duō dà? | polite, to adults |

📎 **Key Points:**
- 几 **jǐ** means 'how many' (for small numbers); 多大 **duō dà** literally means 'how big'.
- No 是 (shì) is needed with age: 我十二岁， not 我是十二岁.

notes.heading: 📅 Dates: Year, Month, Day — 年 / 月 / 日
notes.body:
Chinese dates go **big to small**: year → month → day.

- 年 **nián** = year: 2026年 (years are read digit by digit: èr líng èr liù nián)
- 月 **yuè** = month: 一月 January, 二月 February … 十二月 December (just number + 月)
- 日 **rì** = day: 十八日 the 18th (in speech, 号 **hào** is often used instead)

💡 **Worked Example:**
2026年8月18日 = 18 August 2026 (èr líng èr liù nián bā yuè shíbā rì)

Asking the date: 今天几月几号？Jīntiān jǐ yuè jǐ hào? — What is today's date?

⚠️ **Common Mistake:** English says '18 August' (day first); Chinese always says the month first, then the day. 8月18日, never 18日8月.

notes.heading: 🗓️ Days of the Week — 星期
notes.body:
The week is 星期 **xīngqī**. Weekdays are simply 星期 + a number:

| Chinese | Pinyin | English |
|---|---|---|
| 星期一 | xīngqīyī | Monday |
| 星期二 | xīngqī'èr | Tuesday |
| 星期三 | xīngqīsān | Wednesday |
| 星期四 | xīngqīsì | Thursday |
| 星期五 | xīngqīwǔ | Friday |
| 星期六 | xīngqīliù | Saturday |
| 星期日 / 星期天 | xīngqīrì / xīngqītiān | Sunday |

📎 **Key Points:**
- Monday is day 1 — the numbering starts with Monday, not Sunday.
- Sunday breaks the pattern: it uses 日 (sun) or 天 (sky/day), not 七.
- Useful time words: 今天 jīntiān today, 明天 míngtiān tomorrow, 昨天 zuótiān yesterday.
- Ask the day with: 今天星期几？Jīntiān xīngqī jǐ? — What day is it today?

notes.heading: 🕒 Telling the Time — 点 / 分 / 半
notes.body:
- 点 **diǎn** = o'clock: 三点 sān diǎn = 3:00
- 分 **fēn** = minutes: 三点十五分 sān diǎn shíwǔ fēn = 3:15
- 半 **bàn** = half: 三点半 sān diǎn bàn = 3:30

Asking and answering:
现在几点？Xiànzài jǐ diǎn? — What time is it now?
现在三点。Xiànzài sān diǎn. — It is three o'clock now.

📎 **Key Points:**
- 现在 **xiànzài** means 'now'.
- For 2 o'clock use 两, not 二: 两点 liǎng diǎn.
- Chinese has no am/pm words — add 早上 zǎoshang (early morning), 上午 shàngwǔ (morning), 下午 xiàwǔ (afternoon) or 晚上 wǎnshang (evening) before the time: 下午三点 = 3 pm.

💡 **Worked Example:** 晚上七点半 wǎnshang qī diǎn bàn = 7:30 in the evening.

flashcards.example: 一百零五 yìbǎi líng wǔ = 105. (零 fills the gap in long numbers.)
我有三本书。Wǒ yǒu sān běn shū. (I have three books.)

flashcards.definition: Ten — the building block for numbers 11–99.
Twenty — digit + 十 makes the tens.
Years old — used to state age: number + 岁.
flashcards.example: 我今年十二岁。Wǒ jīnnián shí'èr suì. (I am twelve this year.)
今年是2026年。Jīnnián shì èr líng èr liù nián. (This year is 2026.)
我的生日在五月。Wǒ de shēngrì zài wǔ yuè. (My birthday is in May.)

flashcards.definition: Day (also 'sun'). In speech, 号 hào is often used for the day of the month.
flashcards.example: 今天是八月十八日。Jīntiān shì bā yuè shíbā rì. (Today is 18 August.)

flashcards.definition: Monday — 星期 + 一; the week is numbered from Monday.
flashcards.example: 今天是星期一。Jīntiān shì xīngqīyī. (Today is Monday.)

flashcards.definition: O'clock — number + 点 tells the hour.
flashcards.example: 现在三点。Xiànzài sān diǎn. (It is three o'clock now.)
现在三点半。Xiànzài sān diǎn bàn. (It is half past three now.)

questions.explanation: 五 wǔ is the number five. Counting in order: 一二三四五 = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.
十 shí means ten. It is the building block for 11–99: 十五 is 15, 五十 is 50.

questions.stem: 现在几点？(Xiànzài jǐ diǎn?) is asking:
questions.explanation: 现在 means 'now', 几 means 'how many / which', and 点 means 'o'clock' — together they ask what time it is now.
For 11–19 the pattern is 十 + digit: 十五 = ten-five = 15. Fifty would be 五十 (digit + 十).

questions.stem: How do you say 99 in Chinese?
questions.explanation: Two-digit numbers combine tens and units: 九十九 = nine-ten-nine = 90 + 9 = 99.

questions.stem: 星期一 (xīngqīyī) is which day of the week?
questions.explanation: Weekdays are 星期 + number, counting from Monday: 星期一 is Monday, 星期二 is Tuesday, and so on.

questions.stem: How do you say 'Sunday' in Chinese?
choices: Both 星期日 and 星期天 are correct
questions.explanation: Sunday breaks the numbering pattern: both 星期日 (xīngqīrì) and 星期天 (xīngqītiān) are correct and commonly used. 星期七 does not exist.

questions.stem: 三点半 (sān diǎn bàn) is what time?
questions.explanation: 半 means 'half', so 三点半 is half past three = 3:30.

questions.stem: Which Chinese date correctly says '3 May'?
questions.explanation: Chinese dates go big to small — month before day: 5月3日 (5th month, 3rd day) = 3 May. Putting the day first is an English-order mistake.

questions.stem: Which sentence correctly says 'I am twelve years old'?
questions.explanation: Age is stated without 是: 我 + number + 岁. Adding 是 (我是十二岁) is a common learner error — 是 is not used between a subject and an age.
今 means 'current/this' and 年 means 'year', so 今年 is 'this year' — as in 今年是2026年.

questions.stem: How do you correctly say '2 o'clock' in Chinese?
questions.explanation: Before a measure word like 点, 'two' is 两, not 二: 两点 = 2 o'clock. 二 is used for counting and inside numbers like 十二.
月 means month (and moon). Months are simply numbered: 一月 January, 八月 August.

questions.stem: 昨天 (zuótiān) and 明天 (míngtiān) mean:
questions.explanation: 昨天 is yesterday and 明天 is tomorrow; 今天 is today. These three words appear constantly with dates and plans.
百 means hundred, so 二百 = two-hundred = 200. Twenty would be 二十 (èrshí).
